chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Charlie Johnson's band, Jimmy Harrison and the Harlem trombonists
summary: Danny says Charlie Johnson's band at Small's rivaled Fletcher's, and he and Milt discuss Jimmy Harrison, Big Green and Stump.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: And In New York... He cut everybody in New York. Everybody who thought they could play a trumpet ain't messin'... Him and Jimmy Harrison, they were the two, trombone and trumpet... They were in Charlie Johnson's band, and they're speaking(?) to him, and then Sidney DeParis, and them three... Fletcher Henderson's band didn't have nothin' on Charlie Johnson's band. But Charlie Johnson was working at Small's Paradise, and the difference was that Fletcher was down at the Roseland Ballroom. But them people was out of sight. Jimmy Harrison started all that first position trombone playing.
Yeah, I heard about it. I missed him. I didn't get to hear him. What about Big Green, too? Because I hear so much about him. Did you hear him?
Yes. Great trombone player. Pretty trombone player. There was about ten trombone players. Little Shorty, Little Stump...
He was with Andy Kirk, and he ended up being a messenger around...
Working for Manny's yes. The cat ...(?)...
He was cheeky. The little son-of-a-bitch could play.
I heard Keg Johnson always talk about how good he was.
Yeah, if Keg said it, it had to be so!
Yeah. Well, all of them was in the Brickwood(?).
